chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission (of a slave) for the believer after death.
Nor charity, nor pilgrimage, nor striving (jihad).
Except for what was from a vow or a covenant.

key_terms.جِهَادٌ: Striving/Exertion in the path of God

ai.seo_question: What deeds continue for a believer after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that while general voluntary deeds cease upon death, they continue via the mechanism of *waqf* or specific vows (*nadhr*) and covenants (*ahd*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of spiritual merit through dedicated endowments. This distinction highlights the legal principle that a believer's intent, when formalized through a vow, transforms transient actions into perpetual charity (*sadaqah jariyah*).
